evidence.AC1: POST /todos with {"title":"past","dueDate":"2026-11-01"} returned 201 with dueDate "2026-11-01". POST without dueDate returned 201 with dueDate null. The value is a plain YYYY-MM-DD date. A datetime string ("2026-11-13T10:00:00Z") was rejected with 400.
evidence.AC2: PATCH /todos/2 {"dueDate":"2026-11-02"} returned 200 and the dueDate changed from 2026-12-25 to 2026-11-02. PATCH /todos/1 {"dueDate":null} returned 200 with dueDate null, so the date was removed. I then set it again to 2026-11-01.
evidence.AC3: POST with dueDate "2026-02-30" returned 400. POST with "13/11/2026" returned 400. POST with an ISO datetime returned 400. PATCH with "2026-02-30" returned 400. Each response was {"error":"dueDate must be a date (YYYY-MM-DD) or null"}.
evidence.AC4: Today is 2026-11-13 (UTC). Test data: a todo due 11-01 (not done), one due 11-02 (not done), one due today (11-13), one with no due date, and one due 10-01 that I marked done. GET /todos?overdue=true returned only the 11-02 todo, when todo 1 had its dueDate removed at that moment. That means the done todo, the no-date todo and the due-today todo were all excluded. After I restored todo 1's dueDate to 2026-11-01, the list page showed it as overdue as well, which confirms the past-due, not-done case.
evidence.AC5: The page at / listed each todo with its due date in DD.MM.YYYY format: "past 01.11.2026", "future 02.11.2026", "today 13.11.2026", "pastdone ✓ 01.10.2026". The todo with no due date showed none.
evidence.AC6: In the page snapshot, "past 01.11.2026 überfällig" and "future 02.11.2026 überfällig" carried the word. The "today 13.11.2026" item, the "none" item and the done "pastdone ✓ 01.10.2026" item did not.
evidence.AC7: The page has a checkbox labelled "nur überfällige". Clicking it reduced the list from 5 items to the 2 overdue ones, "past" and "future" (the latter's due date was changed to 11-02).
